summary: This program defines a function that works out what a table owes based on how many items they ordered, then calls it for three different tables and keeps a running total in a cash register variable.

lines.text: len() counts how many items are in the list that was passed in, and each one costs $2. Beepo never needs to know what the items actually are, only how many there were.
This hands the calculated amount back to the main program and ends the function immediately. Without it, the caller would receive None and there would be nothing to add up.
The register starts empty before any tables are visited, so that money can be added to it. Trying to add to a variable that does not exist yet is an error.
The returned amount is caught and added straight into the register. This is the point of a return value: had the result not been stored somewhere, it would simply disappear.
The \n prints a blank line first, separating the three table receipts from the final total. All three calls have finished by now, so the register holds the sum of them all.
